opportunity.title: Jury Management Solution (JMS) System (Presolicitation)
opportunity.agency: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
opportunity.description: Pre-solicitation notice for a web-based Jury Management System for the Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts. The solicitation is unrestricted and not set aside for small business; the Judiciary is not subject to the FAR small business regulations. The AO plans a single-award IDIQ for a commercial off-the-shelf web-based jury management solution that supports selecting, managing and tracking jurors, performs financial and statistical calculations, and interfaces with the Judiciary's financial management system, Momentum. The draft solicitation USCA27R0009 gives requirements and evaluation criteria. The due time is listed as TBD.

supportedClaims.text: The Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts is conducting market research via an RFI to inform a future Jury Management System solicitation.
The RFI requests a commercial off‑the‑shelf, web‑based jury management system that will integrate with the Judiciary’s Momentum financial system.
The vehicle type for the procurement is an Indefinite Delivery Contract.
The opportunity was posted on October 9, 2026, with a response deadline of October 30, 2026.

droppedClaims.text: The presolicitation notice describes a single‑award IDIQ contract for the Jury Management Solution, NAICS 541511, with no set‑aside.
droppedClaims.reason: relevance check: source does not support claim (Source only notes IDV contract and NAICS, not single‑award or set‑aside.)

rationale.point: This is an RFI (market research), not a solicitation; responding positions the company for a future IDIQ competition but does not guarantee award.

The requirement calls for a commercial off‑the‑shelf, web‑based jury management system that integrates with the Judiciary's Momentum financial system — a domain where the company has no demonstrated past performance.

The procurement has no small-business set-aside (full and open), and the agency has zero prior awards in this NAICS, meaning a new entrant would face experienced incumbents without set-aside protection.

risks: No relevant past performance in jury management, court systems, or Momentum integration
Full-and-open competition with no small-business preference
Eleven-person team may lack capacity for IDIQ-scale delivery
No facility clearance limits on-site options
nextSteps: Submit RFI response highlighting analytics and data-system capabilities to shape requirements
Request industry day or one-on-one to assess Momentum integration specifics
Evaluate teaming with a COTS jury-management vendor or a firm with AOUSC past performance
Reassess bid/no-bid when formal solicitation drops, using RFI intelligence

classification.summary: The buyer needs a commercial off‑the‑shelf web‑based jury management system that selects, manages, tracks jurors, performs financial and statistical calculations, and integrates with the Judiciary’s Momentum financial system.
